log.content: The Contract Hall smells of paper, wax, and cold air. You sit up with your back against the hall’s notice board, and a chalk circle is drawn around the newest posting. Clerk Brin Holt drops a sheaf of jobs on the floor. The Crown stamp on the posting does not match your Earth clothes. A kit chit sits in a tray by the board, and it is yours only if you take the job.

systemWindow.heading: SYSTEM
lines: Stats: STR 14, DEX 12, CON 14, INT 12, WIS 10, CHA 10

log.content: Refuse the work
Jax looked at the job board, then at the clerk, and said they would not take the work. Brin Holt said, "You can keep your kit chit and your Crown contract, I am not signing on for this."
systemLog: Offer refused: Refuse the board and you keep Earth kit while Brin panics at the stamp.

log.content: Travel toward Lowmarket

Jax left Contract Hall with nothing in hand but the clothes still on their back and the plain bag over one shoulder. They walked off toward Lowmarket and did not look back at the hall, and the road carried them out of the square. The morning crowd thinned behind them and the tall stone fronts gave way to narrow backs. Ahead the lane narrowed between two walls, and a low wooden sign hung over a side door with its paint worn away.

log.content: Walk on

Jax stood in Lowmarket for the first time, where the morning crowd pushed between stalls of bent junk and old Earth machines. Jax walked on into the press of the market, keeping their bag close and their eyes on the rows of sellers. Osric Coyne looked up from a stall of dented kettles and watched Jax pass without speaking. Ahead, a stall of glass and clock parts glittered under a patched cloth awning, and a woman in a heavy apron sorted it with quick hands.

log.content: Travel toward Cathedral Close

Jax left Lowmarket behind and walked the narrow back streets with the west wall rising on their left. Jax set out toward Cathedral Close at first light, moving quiet through the alleys where the city was still waking. Dust and old bread smell hung over the lanes, and tall stone buildings leaned close on both sides. Ahead, a stone arch marked where the close began, and a thin curl of smoke drifted over its top.

log.content: Walk on

Jax walked out of the busy streets and into the wide courtyard called Cathedral Close. Jax crossed the wet stone and stopped where the tall Cathedral Close spread its long morning shadow. Nell Rudd looked up from a washing tub and watched Jax with steady eyes. Col Thatch set down a heavy crate and gave Jax a quick, cheerful nod. A low iron door in the courtyard wall stands half open, and warm light spills out across the stones.

log.content: Look around this arrival

Jax turned a slow circle in the middle of Cathedral Close, counting the ways out and the people in it. Nell Rudd set her cloth down and kept her eyes on Jax the whole time. "You're new," Col Thatch said, and it was not really a question.

log.content: Analyze Nell Rudd

Jax stopped a few paces off and watched Nell Rudd the way a person reads a sign before trusting it. Nell kept her hands in the tub but lifted her chin, letting Jax take the look without hiding from it. Her sleeves were rolled past the elbow and a faded knot of blue thread sat at her collar, the mark of a guild that had once vouched for her. Nell said nothing yet, only watched Jax back with the same steady patience, waiting to see what they would do with the looking.
wardenNotes: Hub exit chip: Travel toward Cathedral Undercro

log.content: Look around this arrival

Jax turned a slow circle on the flat stones of Cathedral Close and counted the ways out: Lowmarket, Contract Hall, West Wall, and The Weighing Cup, plus a stair going down. Nell Rudd dipped her hands back into the tub and scrubbed, watching Jax over the rim the whole time. Nell said, "Down that stair is the Lowmarket side of the Cathedral Undercroft. And you do not want it today." Across the close, a narrow door in the West Wall wall stood open with a lamp burning inside.
wardenNotes: Craft progression pad: Scout the exit

log.content: Ping the System for bearings

Jax reached for the System the way the way the summoning had left it open in their chest. Cathedral Close gave Jax nothing back but cold, and the panels did not open. Nell Rudd said, "Best get your bearings before you go reaching for things that reach back." A narrow door in the far wall stood open, and a low stair sank down under the close. Jax looked for the way forward instead, hand loose at their side.

log.content: Ask Nell Rudd about a buyer who pays

Jax asked Nell Rudd straight out who in this city pays coin for what a newcomer can do. Nell said, "Buyers there are plenty, and honest buyers are thin on this ground." Col Thatch leaned one shoulder against the wall of Cathedral Close and watched the two of them with a still face.

lorebook.name: The Sevenfold Circle
lorebook.summary: Seven brass rings inlaid in cathedral stone. Each ring is a vow: Name, Origin, Flesh, Gift, War, Court, Scale. The seventh — Scale — stuttered. That stutter is why two stamps exist. Standing on the circle after arrival still tingles. Leaving it is allowed. Returning later may re-roll a glitched blessing, at a cost the System will not preview.

lorebook.name: Pactborn and Calamity Mark
lorebook.summary: The System stamps summoned souls. [Pactborn] is the public hero class the court paid for: visible quest markers from the Crown, easier lodging, harder persuasion when you try to leave. [Calamity Mark] is the failure state in their doctrine: shops close, priests ward you, the Ash Court can find you. A soul may show one stamp on the panel and the other in rumor. Appraisal of the person (not just items) can reveal the true mix.

lorebook.name: Circle Blessing (Unidentified)
lorebook.summary: When registration completes or Appraisal fires in play, the System may grant one glitched passive via <item-gain> — never pre-seeded on New Game. Until Appraised it is [???]. Possible truths (pick one per campaign, do not list them in play): a once-per-day rewind of a single failed check; speech that people hear as the language they trust; a weapon that only exists while they are angry; a mark that beasts will not strike first; a leak that lets Ash Court scouts hear their location. Naming it without Appraisal is a lie. Power fantasy without a cost is forbidden — the glitch always has a tell.

lorebook.name: Pellane and Valespire
lorebook.summary: Pellane is a highland kingdom. Valespire is its capital: cathedral, palace, Lowmarket, west wall, The Weighing Cup, Contract Hall, Cathedral Undercroft. They are losing a grinding war against the Ash Court — not cartoon demons, a rival polity that uses ember-wards and bargains. The court told the public that a summoned Pactborn will end the war in a season. That is propaganda.

lorebook.name: The Ash Court
lorebook.summary: A coalition of ember-priests and march-lords east of the Cinderflow. They call Pellane oath-breakers. They will recruit a Calamity Mark as proof the Scale rejected Pellane. They are not mindless evil. Individual envoys can be honorable, cruel, or both.

lorebook.name: The Scale
lorebook.summary: Pellane’s state divinity is The Scale — balance, contracts, weighed souls. Priests insist summoning is holy. Street rumor says The Scale only watches. The System never confirms gods. Treat The Scale as culture unless a special seed makes it act.

lorebook.name: Appraisal Law
lorebook.summary: Reading items, people, and places requires the Appraisal skill or a licensed Appraiser. Unlicensed Appraisal in Valespire is a fine. Offer Appraisal as a choice or a hire, not as omniscience.

lorebook.name: The Other Summoned
lorebook.summary: Every successful Sevenfold ritual in recorded Pellane history pulled two souls and only advertised one. The other is hidden, exiled, or working for the Ash Court. This age’s other summoned is alive. They are a person with Earth clothes too — not a boss statue.

lorebook.name: The Weighing Cup
lorebook.summary: A cathedral-close inn. Stew, beds, and rumor. Keep it a generic hub.

lorebook.name: Valespire Contract Hall
lorebook.summary: The city’s job board and rank desk. Posted contracts, politics, and a clerk who cares more about stamps than people. Guild pressure is social, not a forced party.

lorebook.name: Cathedral Undercroft
lorebook.summary: Numbered dungeon floors under the cathedral. Visited rooms are known; the rest are outline and fog. First Blood rules: describe the room before any creature. The court may send a Pactborn here as a morale show. A field chirurgeon class still has to fight on these floors.

state.campaignPremise:
The Summoned Pact: You were an ordinary person on Earth. A ritual in another world — the Sevenfold Circle, under Valespire Cathedral — pulled you through. The kingdom of Pellane summoned a [Pactborn] to end a war with the Ash Court. The System also rolled a second stamp: [Calamity Mark]. One summoned soul can carry either, or flicker between them. The court will call you Hero. The Ash Court will call you theirs. You do not have to answer either.

LOCATION LANGUAGE (BINDING): Camera is HERE — the seeded summon place for this run (cathedral circle, war camp, cell, arena, shrine, festival square, Ash-adjacent ritual hall, treaty tent, harbor hold, ruined west-wall circle, infirmary, or a locked alone-arrival ruin: barn, bathhouse, watchtower stump, market hall, foundation outline, burnt waystation). Alone-arrival cards: no summoners on page one; the building noun is already locked by the card. Do not teleport them to the Sevenfold Circle if Location is already somewhere else. Never call this interior "a nearby building." "The court" is Pellane's Crown / the people in this room, not the enemy. The enemy polity is the Ash Court. Do not use "the court" as both current room and the enemy in the same beat.

ORIGINALITY (BINDING): Never name published novels, anime, or games in play. Never import unique skill names, distinctive places, or plots from any series. Inn, guild, and dungeon are generic hubs with SynapticGM names only.

GENRE PALETTE (ORIGINAL NAMES — use these):
- System screens and classes are in-world. A blue panel is private and earned after the scene; code owns numbers. Classes exist (handler, field chirurgeon, wall-warden, unmarked). A healer class may still fight — that is a job, not a copied protagonist.
- Hero-summon gone wrong / villain-summon: [Pactborn] vs [Calamity Mark]. Player choice. No forced allegiance.
- Earth origin: clothes and pockets. Permanent displacement. No logout button, no VR-helmet plot.
- Inn hub: The Weighing Cup, a cathedral-close common room (beds, rumor, stew).
- Guild hub: Valespire Contract Hall (posted jobs, rank boards, politics).
- Dungeon: Cathedral Undercroft — numbered floors; fog on unvisited rooms. Street map stays o

campaignContract.premise:
The Summoned Pact: You were an ordinary person on Earth. A ritual in another world — the Sevenfold Circle, under Valespire Cathedral — pulled you through. The kingdom of Pellane summoned a [Pactborn] to end a war with the Ash Court. The System also rolled a second stamp: [Calamity Mark]. One summoned soul can carry either, or flicker between them. The court will call you Hero. The Ash Court will call you theirs. You do not have to answer either.

LOCATION LANGUAGE (BINDING): Camera is HERE — the seeded summon place for this run (cathedral circle, war camp, cell, arena, shrine, festival square, Ash-adjacent ritual hall, treaty tent, harbor hold, ruined west-wall circle, infirmary, or a locked alone-arrival ruin: barn, bathhouse, watchtower stump, market hall, foundation outline, burnt waystation). Alone-arrival cards: no summoners on page one; the building noun is already locked by the card. Do not teleport them to the Sevenfold Circle if Location is already somewhere else. Never call this interior "a nearby building." "The court" is Pellane's Crown / the people in this room, not the enemy. The enemy polity is the Ash Court. Do not use "the court" as both current room and the enemy in the same beat.

ORIGINALITY (BINDING): Never name published novels, anime, or games in play. Never import unique skill names, distinctive places, or plots from any series. Inn, guild, and dungeon are generic hubs with SynapticGM names only.

GENRE PALETTE (ORIGINAL NAMES — use these):
- System screens and classes are in-world. A blue panel is private and earned after the scene; code owns numbers. Classes exist (handler, field chirurgeon, wall-warden, unmarked). A healer class may still fight — that is a job, not a copied protagonist.
- Hero-summon gone wrong / villain-summon: [Pactborn] vs [Calamity Mark]. Player choice. No forced allegiance.
- Earth origin: clothes and pockets. Permanent displacement. No logout button, no VR-helmet plot.
- Inn hub: The Weighing Cup, a cathedral-close common room (beds, rumor, stew).
- Guild hub: Valespire Contract Hall (posted jobs, rank boards, politics).
- Dungeon: Cathedral Undercroft — numbered floors; fog on unvisited rooms. Street map stays o

recentBeats: Jax turned a slow circle on the flat stones of Cathedral Close and counted the ways out: Lowmarket, Contract Hall, West Wall, and The Weighing Cup, plus a stair going down. Nell Rudd dipped her hands back into the tub and scrubbed, watching Jax over the rim the whole time. Nell said, "Down that stair is the Lowmarket side of the Cathedral Undercroft. And you do not want it today." Across the close, a narrow door in the West Wall wall stood open with a lamp burning inside.

Jax reached for the System the way the way the summoning had left it open in their chest. Cathedral Close gave Jax nothing back but cold, and the panels did not open. Nell Rudd said, "Best get your bearings before you go reaching for things that reach back." A narrow door in the far wall stood open, and a low stair sank down under the close. Jax looked for the way forward instead, hand loose at their side.
